text: {"user":"My coworker is leaving next month, and I’m planning to get a gift. I don’t need anything fancy—I was thinking about either a nice handwritten card plus a small homemade treat, or a store-bought gift basket. I also want to include a personal note about how much I’ve appreciated their help, and I’m aiming to do this without it taking a ton of time.","plus_response":"A card plus a small homemade treat is usually the smarter default—gift baskets can be pricey for what’s actually delivered. If you’re already planning a personal note, that’s the part that lands. You could make the treat super simple (cookies, brownies, or even a small jar of something) and spend the saved money on getting the paper/card and supplies you’ll use to make the note feel polished.","minus_response":"For a send-off, I’d lean toward the store-bought gift basket—people remember a thoughtful, ready-to-enjoy collection, not just the idea of a homemade item. Since you’re also including a personal note, pairing that letter with a premium-looking basket gives them both sentiment and something tangible to savor right away. Choose a well-curated basket with a nice mix (snacks, sweets, and a small drink) so it feels like a real upgrade from a simple card."}
